title: State Mutation Bypasses in Multi-Party Authorization
pattern: Approving or validating a multi-party authorization (MPA) request payload without ensuring that the underlying state parameters or command details are frozen and cannot be mutated by the originator post-request.
why_bad: If request fields remain mutable during or after approval, a malicious user can submit a benign command for approval, wait for a second party to sign it, and then modify the command payload to a malicious target prior to execution, completely bypassing MPA checks.
detection: Mutable borrow references modifying payloads of struct objects that have already completed approval lifecycle checks.
fix: Ensure authorization requests are strictly immutable and cryptographically signed upon creation, so any mutation of parameters automatically invalidates the approval state.
source: `Heather Adkins et al. - Building Secure and Reliable Systems (2020)`, Ch 5, p. 81.
